newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino residents confront anti-APEC protesters.
newsitem.headline: Filipino residents confront anti-APEC protesters.

text.p: About 200 leftist protesters on Thursday marched to the venue of this month's APEC summit in the Philippines but angry residents drove them away, screaming: "We don't need you here."

Dozens of police armed with guns rushed to the scene to block the protesters as they marched on the main Magsaysay Avenue leading to the gate of the Subic Bay freeport, where the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will be held on November 25.
In a shouting match, the protesters chanted slogans such as "APEC is a deception" while about 2,000 shoppers, pedestrians and residents supporting the summit screamed abuse at them, witnesses said.
"Go away," and "We don't need you here," the APEC supporters shouted.

The protesters, who had come in cars and mini-buses from Manila to Olongapo city outside the freeport, marched back to their vehicles and sped out of town to the jeers of residents, according to witnesses.
"This should serve as a warning to those who will try to enter Olongapo uninvited," the city's vice-mayor Cynthia Cajudo told reporters.
"The people of Olongapo have manifested their stand on APEC. We are pro-APEC," she said.

The forum, to be attended by leaders of 18 APEC member economies, will meet in a bullet-proof Leaders Hall inside Subic, a former U.S. naval base which the Philippines turned into an industrial estate after American forces left in 1992.

Police said Thursday's unannounced leftist rally could be a dry-run for at least three protest "people's caravans" to Olongapo, which various anti-APEC groups plan to hold on the day of the summit itself.
Police have vowed to block such protests before they even get close to Subic Bay.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
